source_events.title: Copilot budget increase requests are generally available
source_events.evidence:

You can approve, adjust, or deny that request without leaving your settings.
Requests automatically route to whichever account pays for the budget.

This feature is not available for enterprises with managed users.

stories.headline: Put the agent in the project's environment, and retain session context
stories.what_changed: VS Code added local agent sessions inside a project's Dev Container and expanded Codex session continuity between ChatGPT and VS Code.
stories.why_it_matters: Project-specific tools and dependencies can reduce environment mismatch; preserving the session avoids restarting the conversation. These are workflow recommendations, not measured performance gains.
stories.rationale: Try a noncritical project. Docker and the Agents window are required; rollout is gradual. Containers are not an absolute security boundary, and the AI-generated release notes should be checked against the installed build.

stories.headline: Route Copilot credit requests to the responsible administrator
stories.what_changed: Members who exhaust their Copilot AI credits can request an increase from the paying organization or enterprise; an authorized administrator can approve, adjust, or deny.
stories.why_it_matters: Approval changes the requesting member's budget to the chosen amount. It does not supply free credits or automatically raise the entire organization's budget.
stories.rationale: For Business or Enterprise under usage-based billing, assign an approval owner. The announcement excludes enterprises with managed users; individual subscriptions are outside its scope.

stories.headline: Treat small leaderboard rank differences as hypotheses, not buying decisions
stories.what_changed: A new paper audits historical SWE-bench results rather than evaluating today's newest models.
stories.why_it_matters: Fine-grained ranking can exceed the resolution of the observed verdicts. Non-significance does not prove that models have equal capability.
stories.rationale: Use paired repository evaluations and repeat runs before switching model-plus-harness setups. Findings are author-reported and not independently reproduced.

paper_review.question: Can the observed leaderboard verdicts reliably order the leading coding-agent submissions?
paper_review.method: Observational audit of per-instance verdicts for 254 historical submissions across four SWE-bench splits, retrieved July 30, 2026.
paper_review.result: The authors' paired tests distinguished none of the 29 adjacent Verified top-thirty pairs; this is not proof of equal capability.
paper_review.limitations: Historical submissions from 2023-2025; observational model/scaffold choices; one run per submission; one benchmark family. Results were not independently reproduced.
paper_review.takeaway: Compare model-plus-harness setups on the same representative repository tasks, retain per-task outcomes and versions, repeat runs, and consider cost and latency.
